speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Transport given the ban on users of personal mobility devices from all footpaths, whether there are plans to distinguish the different types of public paths so as to avoid confusion.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether there are plans to regulate the usage of electric bicycles on the roads in terms of age, insurance coverage, traffic rules and others.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The decision to ban e-scooters on footpaths is to restore footpath safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As we step up enforcement, we can expect further reduction in such accidents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: From a recent telephone poll commissioned by the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH), two out of three respondents agreed that safety on footpaths had improved since the ban.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I believe Members of the House would have received similar feedback from friends and residents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Since 1 January this year, LTA has imposed strict enforcement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Those caught riding an e-scooter on footpaths are liable for fines up to $2,000 and/or face imprisonment of up to three months, if convicted.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has expanded its team of active mobility enforcement officers, including Auxiliary Police Officers, from 100 to 182 officers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Recruitment efforts are underway and LTA targets to enlarge the team to 200 soon.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has also deployed technology trials using roving closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras to complement existing enforcement efforts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As of 5 January this year, 27 errant riders have been caught.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are aware that the ban of e-scooters on footpaths has an immediate impact on the livelihoods of some riders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is why we launched the Transition Assistance Package.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This includes the e-scooter trade-in grant (eTG) to help food delivery riders switch to alternative devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are about 6,120 food delivery riders who have done at least one delivery over the 30-day period prior to the ban and are, therefore, eligible for the grant.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Amongst them, about 34%, or 2,100, do four deliveries or more per day.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As of 31 December 2019, LTA has received 3,550 applications from eligible riders and approved all applications after accounting for duplicates.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Twenty percent of these applicants have already transited to alternative devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To facilitate the transition, food delivery companies have offered free bicycle rentals to the riders who are waiting for their new devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Workforce Singapore and the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC’s) Employment and Employability Institute  are providing career placement support for riders who wish to transit to a different job.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and People’s Association have offered temporary financial assistance to affected riders in need.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As some e-scooter users may switch to using power-assisted bicycles (PABs), NTUC launched a fully subsidised safe riding programme to support food delivery riders in making such transition.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As of end-December 2019, 130 riders have completed the NTUC programme.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is useful as on-road accidents involving PABs are not uncommon.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: From January to November last year, there were 21 such accidents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is working with Traffic Police on greater public education and awareness efforts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are updating the regulatory regime for PABs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: All PAB riders must comply with road traffic regulations, such as travelling in the direction of traffic, wearing helmets and riding safely.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Their PABs need to be registered and only LTA-approved models are allowed to be used in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These LTA-approved models are pedal-assisted PABs and without throttles, where gradual motor assistance is provided as the user pedals, but is gradually reduced and cut off as the PAB reaches a speed of 25 kilometres per hour (km/h).

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, they have to comply with the EN15194 device safety standard for electrical and fire safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Since November 2019, we have caught 70 non-compliant PABs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Non-compliant PABs caught will be seized and forfeited.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The offenders can face a maximum fine of $5,000 and/or imprisonment of three months.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Over the last few years, we have strengthened our active mobility regulatory regime, including mandating e-scooter registration.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP) has been a great help.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Government has accepted the latest set of AMAP recommendations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I will shortly introduce a Bill to amend the Active Mobility Act to strengthen the regulatory regime.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This includes setting minimum riding ages, requiring third-party liability insurance coverage and introducing mandatory theory tests.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we are upgrading the cycling infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, we have implemented improved markings on footpaths to clearly distinguish them from cycling paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There will be logos indicating "No PMD" at selected intersections of footpaths and cycling paths to indicate that e-scooters will not be allowed on footpaths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Second, we are stepping up the construction of cycling paths to improve first- and last-mile connectivity within towns.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We had previously announced a plan to extend the network of cycling paths from 440 km to 750 km by 2025 and 1,300 km by 2030.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will accelerate the pace of implementation by a few years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are discussing with the Housing and Development Board (HDB), National Parks Board (NParks) and the local Town Councils on a practical timeline.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are also discussing with our Ministry of Finance (MOF) colleagues to secure additional funding for this purpose.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will provide more details at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I thank the Senior Minister of State for the comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I just want to ask a few supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: He mentioned about 3,000, if I can remember correctly, that have opted for the scheme to convert their e-scooters to other PMDs.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask how many of these are for e-bicycles and others?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The second supplementary question is about the bicycle lane that he had announced.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: He has not announced how many more kilometres; he has just announced that it is being accelerated.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Are you going to increase another 100 km by the end of this year or is this something that is not sure as yet?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the exact number of kilometres of cycling path that we are going to develop by the end of this year, like I have mentioned, we will share more of these details during the Committee of Supply debate.
